 container_name : paperless-ngx-${PAPERLESS_TAG} # Append the image tag to the container name 
 hostname : paperless-ngx # Set the internal application hostname 
 # Apply container labels 
 labels : *disable-watchtower-updates # Paperless upgrades may run database migrations 
 # Define the container environment 
 environment :
 # Broker and database connectivity 
 PAPERLESS_REDIS : ${PAPERLESS_REDIS} # Authenticated Redis broker URL 
 PAPERLESS_DBENGINE : ${PAPERLESS_DBENGINE} # Select the PostgreSQL database backend 
 PAPERLESS_DBHOST : ${PAPERLESS_DBHOST} # PostgreSQL service hostname 
 PAPERLESS_DBNAME : ${POSTGRES_DB} # Paperless database name 
 PAPERLESS_DBUSER : ${POSTGRES_USER} # Paperless database user 
 PAPERLESS_DBPASS : ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD} # Paperless database password 
 # Runtime identity, public URL, and required signing secret 
 USERMAP_UID : ${DEFAULT_UID} # Map Paperless files to the host user 
 USERMAP_GID : ${DEFAULT_GID} # Map Paperless files to the host group 
 PAPERLESS_TIME_ZONE : ${TZ} # Set the Paperless application timezone 
 PAPERLESS_URL : ${PAPERLESS_URL} # Define the canonical public URL 
 PAPERLESS_CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS : ${PAPERLESS_CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS} # Trust the configured reverse proxy origin 
 PAPERLESS_SECRET_KEY : ${PAPERLESS_SECRET_KEY} # Required stable key for signatures and sessions 
 # Initial administrator 
 PAPERLESS_ADMIN_USER : ${PAPERLESS_ADMIN_USER} # Initial administrator username 
 PAPERLESS_ADMIN_PASSWORD : ${PAPERLESS_ADMIN_PASSWORD} # Initial administrator password 
 # Document retention and naming behavior 
 PAPERLESS_EMPTY_TRASH_DIR : ${PAPERLESS_EMPTY_TRASH_DIR} # Trash directory relative to media root 
 PAPERLESS_CONSUMER_DELETE_DUPLICATES : ${PAPERLESS_CONSUMER_DELETE_DUPLICATES} # Remove duplicate consume inputs 
 PAPERLESS_FILENAME_FORMAT : ' {{ created_year }}/{{ correspondent }}/{{ document_type }}/{{ title }} ' # Archive path template 
 # OCR, archive generation, and background processing 
 PAPERLESS_OCR_LANGUAGE : ${PAPERLESS_OCR_LANGUAGE} # Primary OCR language 
 PAPERLESS_OCR_MODE : ${PAPERLESS_OCR_MODE} # Apply the v3 automatic OCR policy 
 PAPERLESS_ARCHIVE_FILE_GENERATION : ${PAPERLESS_ARCHIVE_FILE_GENERATION} # Create archives under the v3 automatic policy 
 PAPERLESS_OCR_ROTATE_PAGES_THRESHOLD : ${PAPERLESS_OCR_ROTATE_PAGES_THRESHOLD} # Rotation confidence threshold 
 PAPERLESS_TASK_WORKERS : ${PAPERLESS_TASK_WORKERS} # Number of background task workers 
 # Office document parsing and conversion 
 PAPERLESS_TIKA_ENABLED : ${PAPERLESS_TIKA_ENABLED} # Enable Office document support 
 PAPERLESS_TIKA_GOTENBERG_ENDPOINT : ${PAPERLESS_TIKA_GOTENBERG_ENDPOINT} # Gotenberg conversion endpoint 
 PAPERLESS_TIKA_ENDPOINT : ${PAPERLESS_TIKA_ENDPOINT} # Apache Tika extraction endpoint 
 # Publish the Paperless web interface 
 ports :
 - ${PAPERLESS_WEBUI_PORT}:8000 # Host port for the Paperless web interface 
 # Mount persistent application directories 
 volumes :
 - ${PAPERLESS_DATA_PATH}:/usr/src/paperless/data:rw # Search index and application data 
 - ${PAPERLESS_MEDIA_PATH}:/usr/src/paperless/media:rw # Documents and generated thumbnails 
 - ${PAPERLESS_EXPORT_PATH}:/usr/src/paperless/export:rw # Document export staging directory 
 - ${PAPERLESS_CONSUME_PATH}:/usr/src/paperless/consume:rw # Incoming document directory 
 - ${PAPERLESS_TRASH_PATH}:/usr/src/paperless/trash:rw # Paperless trash directory 
 # Report healthy when the web application responds successfully 
 healthcheck :
 test : # Request the local application endpoint 
 - CMD 
 - curl 
 - -fsS 
 - --max-time 
 - " 2 " 
 - http://localhost:8000 
 timeout : ${PAPERLESS_HEALTHCHECK_TIMEOUT} # Fail if the check exceeds this duration 
 interval : ${PAPERLESS_HEALTHCHECK_INTERVAL} # Run the check at this interval 
 start_period : ${PAPERLESS_HEALTHCHECK_START_PERIOD} # Allow database migrations and startup work 
 retries : ${PAPERLESS_HEALTHCHECK_RETRIES} # Mark unhealthy after this many failures 
 # Specify container service dependencies 
 depends_on :
 postgres :
 condition : service_healthy # Wait for PostgreSQL readiness 
 redis :
 condition : service_healthy # Wait for authenticated Redis readiness 
 tika :
 condition : service_started # Start the text extraction service first 
 gotenberg :
 condition : service_healthy # Wait for document conversion readiness 
 # 
 # Configure the optional Paperless-AI companion service. 
 # 
 paperless-ai :
 # Docker image and container information 
 << : *default-container # Pull in default container settings 
 image : clusterzx/paperless-ai:${PAPERLESS_AI_TAG} # Run the reviewed Paperless-AI version 
 container_name : paperless-ai-${PAPERLESS_AI_TAG} # Append the image tag to the container name 
 hostname : paperless-ai # Set the internal companion hostname 
 # Drop all Linux capabilities from the companion container 
 cap_drop :
 - ALL # Remove capabilities not required by Paperless-AI 
 # Apply container labels 
 labels : *disable-watchtower-updates # Update the unmaintained companion only after review 
 # Define the container environment 
 environment :
 PUID : ${DEFAULT_UID} # Map companion files to the host user 
 PGID : ${DEFAULT_GID} # Map companion files to the host group 
 # Publish the Paperless-AI web interface 
 ports :
 - ${PAPERLESS_AI_WEBUI_PORT}:3000 # Host port for the Paperless-AI interface 
 # Mount persistent companion configuration 
 volumes :
 - ${PAPERLESS_AI_CONFIG_PATH}:/app/data:rw # Paperless-AI configuration and database 
 # Report healthy when Paperless-AI is configured and its database responds 
 healthcheck :
 test : # Request the upstream application health endpoint 
 - CMD 
 - curl 
 - -fsS 
 - --max-time 
 - " 4 " 
 - http://127.0.0.1:3000/health

 interval : ${PAPERLESS_AI_HEALTHCHECK_INTERVAL} # Run the check at this interval 
 start_period : ${PAPERLESS_AI_HEALTHCHECK_START_PERIOD} # Allow companion initialization work 
 retries : ${PAPERLESS_AI_HEALTHCHECK_RETRIES} # Mark unhealthy after this many failures 
 # Specify container service dependencies 
 depends_on :
 paperless-ngx :
 condition : service_healthy # Wait for the Paperless API to become healthy

 #

 What's the general plan for Paperless-ngx? 
 A: While Paperless-ngx is already considered largely
"feature-complete", it is a community-driven project and development
will be guided in this way. New features can be submitted via
 GitHub discussions 
and "up-voted" by the community, but this is not a
guarantee that the feature will be implemented. This project will always be
open to collaboration in the form of PRs, ideas etc.
 I'm using docker. Where are my documents? 
 A: By default, your documents are stored inside the docker volume
 paperless_media . Docker manages this volume automatically for you. It
is a persistent storage and will persist as long as you don't
explicitly delete it. The actual location depends on your host operating
system. On Linux, chances are high that this location is
 /var/lib/docker/volumes/paperless_media/_data
 Warning
 Do not mess with this folder. Don't change permissions and don't move
files around manually. This folder is meant to be entirely managed by
docker and paperless.
 Note
 Files consumed from the consumption directory are re-created inside
this media directory and are removed from the consumption directory
itself.
 Let's say I want to switch tools in a year. Can I easily move to other systems?
 A: Your documents are stored as plain files inside the media folder.
You can always drag those files out of that folder to use them
elsewhere. Here are a couple notes about that.
 Paperless-ngx never modifies your original documents. It keeps
 checksums of all documents and uses a scheduled sanity checker to
 check that they remain the same.
 By default, paperless uses the internal ID of each document as its
 filename. This might not be very convenient for export. However, you
 can adjust the way files are stored in paperless by
 configuring the filename format .
 The exporter is
 another easy way to get your files out of paperless with reasonable
 file names.
 What file types does paperless-ngx support? 
 A: Currently, the following files are supported:
 PDF documents, PNG images, JPEG images, TIFF images, GIF images and
 WebP images are processed with OCR and converted into PDF documents.
 Plain text documents are supported as well and are added verbatim to
 paperless.
 With the optional Tika integration enabled (see Tika configuration ),
 Paperless also supports various Office documents (.docx, .doc, odt,
 .ppt, .pptx, .odp, .xls, .xlsx, .ods).
 Paperless-ngx determines the type of a file by inspecting its content
rather than its file extensions. However, files processed via the
consumption directory will be rejected if they have a file extension that
is not supported by any of the available parsers.
 Are duplicate documents rejected? 
 A: Not by default. As of v3, a file whose contents match an existing document is still
consumed, and the duplicate is flagged in the UI — open the document and check the
 Duplicates tab to review documents that share the same content, or filter the document
list by Duplicates to find all of them (see
 Duplicate documents ). If you prefer the old
behavior of rejecting duplicates during consumption, set
 PAPERLESS_CONSUMER_DELETE_DUPLICATES 
to true .
 Will paperless-ngx run on Raspberry Pi? 
 A: The short answer is yes. I've tested it on a Raspberry Pi 3 B.
The long answer is that certain parts of Paperless will run very slow,
such as the OCR. On Raspberry Pi, try to OCR documents before feeding
them into paperless so that paperless can reuse the text. The web
interface is a lot snappier, since it runs in your browser and paperless
has to do much less work to serve the data.
 Note
 You can adjust some of the settings so that paperless uses less
processing power. See setup for details.
 How do I install paperless-ngx on Raspberry Pi? 
 A: Docker images are available for arm64 hardware, so just
follow the Docker Compose instructions . Apart from more required disk
space compared to a bare metal installation, docker comes with close to
zero overhead, even on Raspberry Pi.
 If you decide to go with the bare metal route, be aware that some of
the python requirements do not have precompiled packages for ARM /
ARM64. Installation of these will require additional development
libraries and compilation will take a long time.
 Note
 For ARMv7 (32-bit) systems, paperless may still function, but it could require
modifications to the Dockerfile (if using Docker) or additional
tools for installing bare metal. It is suggested to upgrade to arm64
instead.
 How do I run this on Unraid? 
 A: Paperless-ngx is available as community
app in Unraid. Uli
Fahrer created a container template for that.
 How do I run this on my toaster? 
 A: I honestly don't know! As for all other devices that might be
able to run paperless, you're a bit on your own. If you can't run the
docker image, the documentation has instructions for bare metal
installs.
 Does Paperless-ngx use AI, and is my data private? 
 A: Paperless-ngx includes optional AI features — LLM-based suggestions, document chat,
and similar-document retrieval — that are disabled by default . They only run when you
enable them and configure an LLM backend. The built-in tag/correspondent suggestions use a
local, non-LLM machine-learning model and do not send your data anywhere. If you enable the
LLM features, document content is sent to whichever backend you configure — this can be a
fully local backend (e.g. Ollama) or a remote provider. See
 AI features for details.
 Which message broker should I use ?
 Paperless-ngx talks to a Redis-compatible message broker, so any broker that
implements the Redis protocol will work. The bundled Docker Compose files
default to Valkey , the open-source fork created after
Redis' licensing change, but Redis itself and other wire-compatible brokers
(such as Microsoft's Garnet) are equally fine.
 Existing installs can switch broker implementations in place: point
 PAPERLESS_REDIS at the new instance and
reuse the same data volume.
